claims.statement: Open SWE's backend is a LangGraph application that registers three graphs (agent, reviewer, review-scout) together with a FastAPI app (openswe.webapp:app), all wired through langgraph.json which declares the Python version (3.14), LangGraph API version (>~=0.15.0rc1), registered graphs, checkpointer TTL policy (60-minute sweep, 43,200-minute default TTL with delete strategy), and loads .env.

make dev runs `uv run langgraph dev --no-browser --port 2024 --n-jobs-per-worker 10`, serving all three graphs plus the FastAPI app on http://localhost:2024 so that both the /webhooks/* and /dashboard/api/* endpoints are available from one process; a local PostgreSQL 16 container is started automatically unless POSTGRES_URI is set.

make run runs `uvicorn openswe.webapp:app --reload --port 8000` and serves the FastAPI app without the LangGraph runtime, which is insufficient for dashboard features that create LangGraph runs; full local dev therefore requires make dev on :2024.

make install installs backend dependencies including dev extras via `uv sync --extra dev`, and the Makefile exposes uv-run wrappers for pytest (test/integration_tests), ruff (lint/format/format-check), ty (typecheck) over the repository or openswe and tests.

The local dev server's LangGraph constraints are set to langgraph-api>=0.16.1,<0.17 and langgraph-runtime-inmem>=0.36.1,<0.37 in pyproject.toml (as constraint-dependencies), while langgraph.json declares api_version >~=0.15.0rc1; the standalone Docker image uses langchain/langgraph-api:0.15.1-py3.14 base with environment variable registrations for graphs and checkpointer instead of manifest declarations.

The desktop app connects to a shared backend; langgraph.desktop.json is no longer used. Local development uses the standard LangGraph manifest to serve the agent and other graphs for desktop clients that connect via the bridge protocol on the same backend that web clients reach.

make web runs `pnpm run dev --filter=open-swe-dashboard` (via root package.json), starting the dashboard Vite dev server on http://localhost:3000, which in development proxies backend paths to DASHBOARD_API_URL (defaulting to http://localhost:2024) so no ui/.env is needed.

The dashboard build/typecheck/test/check scripts fan out across the workspace through Turborepo, while root lint (oxlint) and format/format:check (oxfmt) scripts run once from the repo root and are not Turborepo tasks.

Turborepo's build task caches .output/**, .vercel/output/**, and build/**, and treats DASHBOARD_API_URL, SOURCE_COMMIT, VERCEL, E2E_HARNESS, and any VITE_* variable as cache-affecting build inputs so changing them invalidates cached builds.

The experimental Electron desktop app bundles the compiled dashboard UI and a local backend connection; it connects to a selected cloud backend URL for cloud-connected threads and supports local-agent work on This Mac through a shared loopback LangGraph server; packaged builds ask for and store a backend URL rather than defaulting to a hosted deployment.

make install-desktop installs or updates Open SWE Desktop on macOS by refusing to run with a dirty working tree, fast-forwarding to main, then invoking scripts/install_desktop.sh, whereas make install-checkout runs that script against the current checkout without touching git state.

scripts/install_desktop.sh is macOS-only, verifies node, ditto, bun, and a pnpm/corepack launcher are present, packs the desktop app with `pnpm --dir desktop run pack`, and atomically swaps it into /Applications or ~/Applications when /Applications is not writable.
scripts/create_sandbox_snapshot.py builds a LangSmith sandbox snapshot from a Docker image using SandboxClient and prints the resulting UUID to set as DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID.

scripts/purge_wakeup_crons.py is a one-time backfill that deletes expired one-shot thread_wakeup crons from a deployment, resolving the deployment URL from --url/LANGGRAPH_URL and the API key from LANGGRAPH_API_KEY/LANGSMITH_API_KEY.

The root Dockerfile builds the standalone production LangGraph API server image from langchain/langgraph-api:0.15.1-py3.14, installing the repository with uv and baking the three graph registrations (via LANGSERVE_GRAPHS), HTTP app (via LANGGRAPH_HTTP), and checkpointer TTL (via LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINTER) into environment variables; it exposes port 8000.

A standalone backend container requires the Agent Server backing services and settings — DATABASE_URI (Postgres), REDIS_URI (Redis), LANGSMITH_API_KEY, and LANGGRAPH_CLOUD_LICENSE_KEY — plus LANGGRAPH_URL set to the public backend URL, and must not use scale-to-zero hosting because background runs rely on Redis/Postgres-backed workers staying available.

ui/Dockerfile is a multi-stage Node 24 Alpine build (run from the repo root) that installs the frozen pnpm workspace, builds open-swe-dashboard into a Nitro .output server, runs it as user node on port 8080, and reads the backend it fronts from DASHBOARD_API_URL at runtime so one image serves any deployment.

In a separate dashboard deployment, the dashboard proxies browser /dashboard/api/* requests and /webhooks/* deliveries to the backend and forwards the osw_session cookie on server renders, making requests same-origin when DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL and the GitHub App callback are set to the dashboard origin; a cross-origin alternative points the browser at the backend via VITE_DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL and requires the dashboard origin in DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

The backend can alternatively be deployed to LangGraph Platform by connecting the repository and setting the same application environment, using the hosted deployment URL for LANGGRAPH_URL and webhook callbacks.

The production Nitro proxy requires DASHBOARD_API_URL at request time and throws if it is unset, rather than falling back to a backend; it proxies the original path and query while preserving OAuth redirects manually.

The backend can serve a bundled dashboard from DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR or an in-repository ui/.output/public build, while explicitly declining reserved API and LangGraph paths so its UI catch-all cannot shadow them; a configured Vite development URL replaces the static build for same-origin hot reload.

Dashboard asset and client-router paths must be built with DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH equal to a LangGraph http.mount_prefix; the platform manifest derives that build value from its mount_prefix, while local builds require it to be supplied.

make tunnel requires NGROK_DOMAIN and exposes local port 2024 through an ngrok traffic policy that returns 404 for every path outside /webhooks/*, protecting unauthenticated LangGraph development routes from public exposure.

The root Docker image does not itself build the dashboard; standalone Docker serving needs a prebuilt dashboard in the repository or DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR, whereas the platform manifest (langgraph.json dockerfile_lines) performs a best-effort dashboard build and continues backend deployment if it fails.

A standalone backend using LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop exposes raw LangGraph routes to network clients; deployments should use LangSmith authentication or an authenticated/private network boundary because dashboard sessions and webhook signatures protect only custom routes.

The FastAPI lifespan startup sequence validates configuration, pins an event loop, acquires a database advisory lock, creates the open_swe schema and runs alembic migrations, imports workspace data from the LangGraph Store into Postgres (idempotent steps), deletes legacy analyzer crons, syncs admin flags, starts an analytics worker, starts transcript/bridge/UI-invalidation/notification listeners, warms the agent build, and opens LangGraph graphs; import/analytics/listener failures log warnings but do not prevent startup.

The local PostgreSQL container (open-swe-postgres) is started by make dev when POSTGRES_URI is unset, binds only to loopback 127.0.0.1:5433, and persists data in the open-swe-postgres named volume so local data survives container restarts.

make dev-ui starts the Vite dev server on port 3000 and the LangGraph backend on port 2024 in parallel, passing DASHBOARD_DEV_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000 to the backend so it reverse-proxies UI requests to Vite while keeping the browser on the FastAPI origin for API calls and login.

The bundled dashboard build (ui/.output/public) contains a client-only _shell.html entry point and hashed immutable assets; the server serves hashed assets with max-age=31536000,immutable and the shell with no-cache so new builds can be picked up.

The Electron desktop app's dev flow uses an isolated 'Open SWE Development' profile so it can run alongside an installed app without sharing login, backend config, or projects; source launches default to http://localhost:2024 or accept --backend-url/OPEN_SWE_BACKEND_URL.

Alembic-based database migrations in openswe/database/migrations/versions/ run at startup within an advisory lock (XID 557314367248862439), create the open_swe schema if missing, and execute only new revisions tracked in alembic_version; on the preview environment, rebased branch heads that become superseded are deleted from the version table to apply the new chain cleanly.

LangGraph checkpointer configuration declares a delete strategy with 60-minute sweep intervals and 43,200-minute (30-day) default TTL; threads restarting within 60 minutes preserve checkpoint state, beyond which checkpoints are eligible for deletion, and multiple replicas share checkpoint storage so a failed replica can resume threads on another as long as database and Redis remain available.

The backend exposes GET /health returning {"status": "healthy"} and POST /webhooks/run-complete for token-verified run completion; neither performs database connectivity checks, and deployments using scale-to-zero hosting are unsupported because background runs rely on Redis and Postgres workers staying available.

Multiple replicas share Postgres for state and Redis for workers; cross-replica communication includes transcript listener (Store writes), sandbox-bridge listener (file I/O), analytics worker (Store-to-Postgres), UI invalidation hub (dashboard updates), and database notification listener (PostgreSQL NOTIFY), with listener startup failures logged as warnings that allow the replica to continue with degraded feature support.
